content:
lately every time I run lake exe cache get or lake update or anything similar on macOS (m5), cache always fails with 

.../.cache/mathlib/dc24ed26db372d4f.ltar: Too many open files (os error 24) at path "../Projects/Lean/cslib/.lake/packages/mathlib/./.lake/..."
...(repeats)

The best solution I have so far is ulimit -n 10240, but this is not very ideal. This number 10240 is the highest useful number according to apple's forum. So this method only works until cache needs to "open" more files.
Does "lately" mean days or weeks? Can you correlate to a particular toolchain version? How many cores (sysctl hw.ncpu) do you have? What's your default ulimit -n?

So this method only works until cache needs to "open" more files.

The likely culprit is leantar, and the problematic upper bound is roughly core countx file count in a .ltar archive, so ulimit -n 10240should always be enough as a workaround.

Indeed, file count in a .ltar archive grows as lean has more relevant output files (e.g. with the module system). Mathlib ltars currently have 13-16 files, so with >16 cores one can go over the limit. digama0/leangz#10 reduces the number of file descriptors held by leantar (making it independent of archive filecount) to fix it (cc @Mario Carneiro )
yeah leantar is the offending program here. It opens too many files and the reason I am probably facing it now might have something to do with the increase in mathlib's size.
Lately = last two weeks. I did not check the default value. I directly tried ulimit -n 100000 and then had to search to find out why it didn't work
Turns out macOS doesn't care for values larger than 10240 according to that post on apple's forums. Fortunately 10240 was sufficient
Yep that makes sense. As a workaround while the fix is adopted you can put the ulimit line in your shell rc (~/.zshrc, I suppose) to make it stick across terminals
Thanks. I looked online and it seems that the default ulimit soft limit might be 256 and the hard limit is 10240
